To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there are many different correctness statements about safety, (2) the different correctness statements are related to each other, and (3) the different statements are not equivalent, and thus, they are not interchangeable.

(1) correctness statements about microprocessor implementations and specifications are classified as safety properties, (2) the correctness of an implementation with respect to a specification is a safety property, (3) safety properties can be characterized by the set of possible behaviors of the implementation, the set of possible states of the implementation, and the set of possible events, (4) the correctness of a specification is a special case of a safety property, where the set of possible implementations is empty,

the different correctness statements have different properties, and that the choice of correctness statement should be driven by the desired verification properties.
